India's approach to artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence has applications in education, agriculture, healthcare, language access and public administration. Government initiatives may support AI research, computing facilities, datasets, skills and practical applications.

For examination purposes, it is important to distinguish a national mission from a language platform, a model-development initiative, a state-level centre and a proposal invitation. Their purposes and documented stages of implementation are different.

The programme facts below are presented using official announcements available up to the content cutoff of 4 November 2026. Dates and financial amounts refer to the specified government announcements, not to an independently verified later expenditure or project-completion total.

IndiaAI Mission

The Union Cabinet approved the IndiaAI Mission on 7 March 2024 with a financial outlay of ₹10,371.92 crore. The mission is implemented by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). Its broad purpose is to strengthen India's AI ecosystem and support inclusive, socially useful and responsible AI development.

A Press Information Bureau release dated 30 July 2026 identified the following 7 pillars:

  • IndiaAI Compute Capacity: Expanding access to the computing resources needed for AI development.
  • IndiaAI Innovation Centre: Supporting the development of indigenous AI models and related innovation.
  • IndiaAI Datasets Platform: Improving access to useful datasets and model resources, including the AIKosh platform.
  • IndiaAI Application Development Initiative: Encouraging AI applications that address practical needs.
  • IndiaAI Future Skills: Supporting education, training and skill development in AI.
  • IndiaAI Startup Financing: Supporting AI-related startup development.
  • Safe & Trusted AI: Supporting approaches that address reliability, safety and responsible use.

Computing infrastructure and datasets make AI development easier, while skills, applications, financing and safety measures address other requirements. The mission is therefore broader than the development of a single chatbot or language model.

BHASHINI: AI for Indian languages

BHASHINI is an Indian initiative that uses language technologies to reduce barriers to digital services. It supports uses such as machine translation and speech-related services in Indian languages.

Government information published in 2025 records its launch in July 2022. Its importance lies in improving access for people who may find a digital service difficult to use in another language.

For example, a speech or translation service may help a citizen understand information presented in a different Indian language. However, names, official terminology and important instructions still require accuracy checks. Translation generated by AI is not automatically an authoritative legal or administrative interpretation.

BharatGen: Indian-language foundation models

BharatGen is a government-supported initiative for developing indigenous AI models suited to Indian languages and contexts. The initiative was inaugurated on 30 September 2024; its multimodal LLM was launched at the BharatGen Summit on 2 June 2025.

The initiative covers multimodal AI capabilities, meaning the development of models that can work with different forms of information, including text, speech and visual material.

Official statements described plans to expand its Indian-language coverage. A stated target for future language support should not be confused with proof that every planned language capability was already fully operational at the time of the announcement.

BHASHINI is associated particularly with language access and translation-related services. BharatGen is associated with developing Indian-language foundation AI models. They are related to language technology but are not identical initiatives.

Gujarat: AI Centre of Excellence at GIFT City

The Government of Gujarat established an Artificial Intelligence Centre of Excellence (AI CoE) at GIFT City, Gandhinagar. A Department of Science and Technology circular approved on 13 February 2026 states that the centre was launched on 27 January 2025.

The circular describes the centre's role in encouraging responsible AI adoption, innovation and applications for government departments and public-service delivery. It also identifies collaboration with Gujarat Informatics Limited (GIL) and other partners.

The same circular concerns an AI Innovation Challenge intended to encourage solutions for government use cases. The existence of the challenge does not establish that every proposed solution had already been developed or deployed.

Gujarati-language large language model proposal

In 2025, Gujarat Informatics Limited invited an Expression of Interest (EOI) for the design and development of an indigenous large language model for the Gujarati language. Its published tender details recorded a pre-bid meeting on 10 June 2025 and a bid-submission deadline of 21 July 2025.

An EOI invites proposals from interested organisations. It is not equivalent to the launch of a completed model. This distinction matters when evaluating statements about the progress of a public technology project.

Programme timeline

Connecting the programmes with basic AI concepts

The IndiaAI Mission addresses conditions that support AI development, such as computing, datasets and skills. BHASHINI applies language technology to improve access. BharatGen is concerned with developing reusable AI models. Gujarat's AI Centre of Excellence supports state-level innovation and public-service applications. These initiatives illustrate different parts of the same AI ecosystem.

The foundational concepts remain essential when using these programmes: machine learning develops models from data; trained models produce outputs during inference; generative systems may produce plausible but incorrect material; and responsible use requires privacy protection, fairness and human oversight.

Prelims focus

  • IndiaAI Mission: approved on 7 March 2024; announced outlay of ₹10,371.92 crore; implemented by MeitY.
  • The IndiaAI Mission has 7 pillars, including Compute Capacity, Datasets Platform, Future Skills and Safe & Trusted AI.
  • BHASHINI supports AI-based Indian-language access and translation; its launch was recorded as July 2022.
  • BharatGen was inaugurated on 30 September 2024 as an Indian-language AI model-development initiative; its multimodal LLM was launched on 2 June 2025.
  • Gujarat's AI Centre of Excellence at GIFT City, Gandhinagar, was launched on 27 January 2025.
  • GIL invited an EOI for an indigenous Gujarati-language LLM in 2025.
  • Trap: Approval, launch, invitation of proposals and completed operational deployment are different stages.

[Sources: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, 'Cabinet Approves Ambitious IndiaAI Mission to Strengthen the AI Innovation Ecosystem,' 7 March 2024; Press Information Bureau, 'Government of India Promotes AI and Digital Tech Adoption to Boost MSME Productivity,' 30 July 2026, IndiaAI Mission and its 7 pillars; Press Information Bureau, 'Bhashini: Voice for Digital Inclusion,' section on BHASHINI, published 2025; Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Science and Technology, 'Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh launches Bharat Gen,' 2 June 2025; Press Information Bureau, 'Parliament Question: BharatGen AI Models,' 6 August 2025, language-coverage status and roadmap; Government of Gujarat, Department of Science and Technology, Circular No. DST/AIE/e-file/24/2025/1433/E-Governance, approved 13 February 2026, p. 1; Gujarat Informatics Limited, 'Tender Details: Inviting Expression of Interest for Design and Development of Indigenous Large Language Model for Gujarati Language,' 2025, bid details. All online sources consulted 4 November 2026.]

title: AI Initiatives in India and Gujarat: Programmes, Dates and Key Distinctions
